rationale: Every rule in hermeticity-rules.json has a planted defect here and an exact expected count. The test compares the prober's output to these counts, so a rule that silently stops firing fails the suite instead of quietly reporting a clean tree.
expected_advisory_note: anchored_import_path.py is the only fixture that must not fail the gate. It plants the accepted form of import-path mutation in all three shapes the tree uses -- direct, through one __file__-derived root, and through a chain of them -- so the downgrade is proved rather than asserted. Its unanchored counterpart in import_path_mutation.py still fires at full severity, which is what stops the downgrade from being a hole.

workstreams/po03/runtime/fixtures/litera.why: Every literal matches a rule regex and none is a path the program uses. All eight roles must be exercised, because a role that never classifies anything is untested code deciding what to suppress.

The guard on the TEST_FIXTURE role, which is the widest of the eight. Every literal here sits in an asserting test method in a test_*.py file and every one still fires, because each reaches a filesystem sink. A test module is not a blanket exemption.

rules_without_a_committed_fixture_note: PARSE_ERROR is proved with a synthetic unparseable source built inside the test. Committing a file that does not parse would break unrelated tooling that walks the tree.
